open_points.subject: _build_approved_snapshot and import_snapshot timestamp handling
open_points.text: - _build_approved_snapshot: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST copy estimate_id, estimate_version, project_id, approved_at, approved_by, currency, tax_mode, sections, source_system, published_at and contract_version from the same-named fields of the publication, every field the publication carries, into a new immutable snapshot without Registry name or address fields; it MUST take content_fingerprint from the fingerprint argument, received_at from the received_at argument, the one timestamp the attempt captured, received_from from the service_principal_id of the actor, received_key_version from the key_version of the actor, and snapshot_id fresh as its identifier note requires; source_type and scope_mode of the actor are not carried.
open_points.other_text: - import_snapshot: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it creates and every current-time comparison it makes; the publication's `approved_at` and `published_at` are copied as published, never replaced by it; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself. A supplied `approved_at` or `published_at` that carries a UTC offset MUST be converted to UTC, keeping its instant, before it is stored offset-naive; a supplied offset-naive value is taken as UTC.
open_points.question: Must _build_approved_snapshot copy approved_at and published_at unchanged from its publication argument, or must it transform offset-aware values to offset-naive UTC before storing them?
